Synopsis:
    A U.S. federal appeals court struck down a Trump administration DOE emergency order that had forced Michigan's J.H. Campbell coal plant to stay online past its planned retirement. The court ruled DOE exceeded its authority under the Federal Power Act. The plant's forced operation cost Consumers Energy ~$295M over ~13 months. The utility will continue operating the plant under a current 90-day DOE order while reviewing the ruling. The decision challenges the administration's broader strategy of using emergency powers to keep aging coal plants running amid rising U.S. electricity demand driven by data center expansion.
